subject: Renewal uptick & accelerator package - term sheet and price hold request
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brightbuy.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Anika Bose <anika.bose@brightbuy.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + short-term capacity sprint

Jordan —

Thanks for the check-in last week. As we start planning our FY27 roadmap, we expect a product push in Q4 that will require a 40–60% uplift in inference capacity for 6–8 weeks. We want to lock in a renewal now (12-month) but add a short-term accelerated capacity package to cover the sprint. High-level asks: 

- Price hold on current committed unit price through the renewal term (we need predictability for finance)
- A temporary uplift bucket (prepaid capacity) that we can burn over Q4 (6–8 weeks)
- One-time operational credit to offset migration validation costs

Can you share what flexible renewal constructs Redwood can offer? If possible we want to avoid a multi-month pricing negotiation later this fall — hoping to finalize by end of August.

Attached: our Q2 usage export for your reference.

Best,
Rajiv
Director of Platform Engineering
BrightBuy Retail

Attachments: BrightBuy_Usage_Q2_2026.csv (CSV, 74KB)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brightbuy.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + short-term capacity sprint

Rajiv —

Appreciate the context and the usage file. We can absolutely support an accelerated capacity package alongside your 12-month renewal. Proposal outline I want to validate with you before we draft a formal term sheet: 

1) Renewal term: 12 months, start 2026-10-01
2) Price hold: current unit rate held for the 12-month term if commit stays within +/-15% of prior-year consumption; beyond that we layer a usage true-up at a reduced incremental rate
3) Sprint bucket: one-time prepaid accelerator (equivalent of 6 weeks at 1.5x baseline throughput) redeemable within Q4 2026; unused capacity can be converted into on-demand credits at a fixed conversion rate
4) Operational credit: one-time $15k credit to help with migration and validation testing

If that aligns, I’ll get Ben to draft the term sheet and loop in Legal for a short amendment. Can you confirm: 1) the target start/end dates for the sprint (tentative), and 2) whether finance needs the price-hold reflected in an invoice schedule or the contract language?

I’ll aim to get a PDF term sheet back to you by Tuesday.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0143

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brightbuy.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: BrightBuy draft term sheet (v3) — accelerator + price hold

Rajiv / Anika —

Attached is a first draft term sheet (v3) capturing Jordan's outline. Highlights: 

- 12-month renewal starting 2026-10-01; committed baseline = prior 12m consumption normalized to rolling 30-day averages
- Price hold: unit price held for the term provided consumption variance <=15% vs baseline; incremental consumption billed at a capped overage rate (20% discount vs current on-demand)
- Accelerator pack: prepaid bucket equal to 6 weeks at 1.5x baseline throughput; valid 2026-10-15 through 2026-12-31; unused portion convertible to credits at 70% face value
- Operational credit: $15,000 (applied as invoice credit on first renewal invoice)
- True-up cadence: quarterly; invoices include line-item for any conversion/true-up adjustments

We attached the term sheet + brief redlines doc. A couple of notes for you: 
- Legal prefers the price-hold language tied to the variance band (<=15%) to avoid open-ended exposure. 
- If you'd like a guaranteed upper ceiling for burstable overages (instead of a capped overage %), we can propose a tiered ceiling as an addendum.

Next steps: please review and mark any points you want tightened. If this looks good, Jordan will prepare an executive summary for approval and we’ll kick off DocuSign routing.

Attachments: BrightBuy_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (PDF, 48 pages), TermSheet_Redlines_BB_v3.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brightbuy.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Anika Bose <anika.bose@brightbuy.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBuy draft term sheet (v3) — accelerator + price hold

Ben / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few requests from Procurement and Finance: 

- Can the price hold be explicit on invoice schedule (finance needs it reflected), not just contract language.
- The 15% variance makes sense; can we add a one-time tolerance of +10% for expected Q4 marketing spikes? In short: allow the sprint to exceed 15% without triggering the higher overage rate once (only for the prepaid accelerator period).
- For the unused accelerator conversion, would you consider 80% credit conversion instead of 70%? That helps our CFO with forecasting conservatively.

If you can accept the invoice reflection + the one-time tolerance and nudge the conversion to 80%, we can get approvals on our side and route to DocuSign. We're aiming to have this signed by 8/31 so engineering can plan.

Also: please include references to SOC2 logging and audit evidence in the appendix; our audit team will ask.

Regards,
Rajiv

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@brightbuy.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBuy draft term sheet (v3) — accelerator + price hold

Rajiv —

Great — we can accommodate the three items you flagged. Summary of concessions we agreed to internally and are now adding to the term sheet: 

1) Price-hold reflection: explicit invoice schedule line added (line 2) confirming unit rate held for the renewal invoice(s).
2) One-time Q4 tolerance: additive one-time variance of +10% above the 15% band for the accelerator window (2026-10-15 through 2026-12-31) — this will not trigger the capped overage rate for that single tolerance event.
3) Accelerator conversion: unused capacity converts to account credits at 80% face value.

We also added an appendix referencing SOC 2 Type II evidence and the audit contact for Production logs — Monica is copied for the evidence handoff and will share the secure Drive link once Legal finishes the appendix. 

Ben updated the term sheet and Legal has approved the final language. Please sign via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4892 — Jordan will update the close date once signed.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute handoff between your infra and our SRE team next week to validate the burst patterns.

Looking forward to getting you squared away for Q4.

— Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0143

Attachments referenced: BrightBuy_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (final), SOC2_Evidence_Appendix.pdf (stub)
